acceptance: The close-wave unit tests prove named source tickets are captured and a close-wave receipt cannot be successful unless every expected ticket is fixed, CONFIRMED-FIXED, and linked by a non-empty fixed_by; the focused test command exits 0.
acceptance_cmd: uv run --no-project --python 3.13 --with pytest pytest -q ops/tests/test_worktree_orchestrate.py -k expected_ticket
acceptance_green_expected: The current primary lacks the new invariant and the focused regression tests are expected to be red before this worktree patch is landed.
brief: Delivery closure can report success while the tickets it was meant to close remain open, misleading the team count.
detail: close-wave can return rc=0 after Gate, cutover, anchor and validate while its named source reservations have no staged closure rows, leaving the expected tickets triaged and CONFIRMED-OPEN. Wave-2 exposed this when three landed source branches were resolved and anchor applied an empty set.
plan: Derive the expected ticket ids from the named source reservations in the worktree registry and persist them in the close-wave manifest before source teardown. Refuse a committed close-wave when that set is empty. After anchor, read each expected backlog entry and require status=fixed, verdict=CONFIRMED-FIXED, and a non-empty fixed_by list before validate, teardown, or sync can lead to rc=0. Apply the same check to completed and validated recovery paths, emit the exact ids and failures in receipts, and add focused RED/GREEN tests for foreign branches, empty sets, missing entries, wrong verdicts, and missing fixed_by.
scope: one orchestrator guard, its regression tests, and a verified closure receipt.
verified_evidence: uv run --no-project --python 3.13 --with pytest pytest -q ops/tests/test_worktree_orchestrate.py -k expected_ticket (4 passed)
